items: One way of organizing classes is through **inheritance**.
Inheritance allows objects of a class to take on the properties of objects from another class.
**Inheritance is used to avoid the repetition of programming instructions for each class.**
To apply inheritance between classes, the **`extends`** keyword is used.

blocks.value: A `Student` **is a** `Person`. Everything a `Person` has, a `Student` has automatically, plus whatever it adds.
Without inheritance, `Student`, `Teacher`, and `Staff` would each repeat `name` and `age` and every method that uses them. Inheritance writes it once.
A subclass object can use the fields it inherits as if it had declared them itself:

Student pupil = new Student();     // Student extends Person
pupil.name = "Ana";                 // inherited from Person
pupil.studentNumber = 7;            // declared in Student
System.out.println(pupil.name + " " + pupil.studentNumber);   // Ana 7
